title: Semester and Mixtape
premise: Mirabel Villalobos just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built on the ruins of an old amusement park whose founder vanished decades ago. When her first real friend, Juniper, disappears and leaves behind a ring of keys tied to the park's buried past, Mirabel is dragged into a mystery that runs beneath the school itself — and into a rivalry with the debate-and-quiz team captain, Theo, who knows more than he admits. To find Juniper, Mirabel must win the state quiz championship everyone's watching, and the secret tournament of keys hidden in the school's foundations, before the final game of the season seals the underground forever. She wins both, saves Juniper, and chooses her found family over the inheritance she was never supposed to claim.
about_author: Lior Brightwater grew up in a rust-belt town where the mall swallowed an old drive-in theater, and has been writing about what gets paved over ever since. They teach creative writing to teenagers and still keep every mixtape they've ever been handed.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On her first day at Hollow Creek High, she maps the exits, memorizes the social hierarchy, and vows invisibility. But she can't help noticing the school hums at odd hours, like something underneath is tuning itself. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, cracked slightly by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl with the Walkman
chapters.summary: Juniper Okafor bulldozes into Mirabel's carefully invisible life, handing her a hand-labeled mixtape like it's a contract. Their friendship ignites over lunch-table contraband and rumors about the school being built atop the old Meridian Park amusement grounds. POV: Mirabel. Beat: reluctant warmth becoming real belonging.

chapters.title: What the Foundation Remembers
chapters.summary: During a basement detention, Mirabel hears music through the floor — a song from Juniper's tape. The janitor, Mr. Sable, warns her some doors were sealed for reasons. POV: Mirabel. Beat: unease; the school is not just a building.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Juniper vanishes between sixth period and morning. Police call it a runaway; her locker holds only a ring of seven brass keys stamped MERIDIAN. Mirabel, the last person who saw her, keeps the keys instead of turning them in. POV: Mirabel. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Theo Reyes Has Answers
chapters.summary: Quiz team captain Theo corners Mirabel — not to accuse her, but because Juniper had been asking him about Meridian Park too. Their alliance begins as mutual suspicion. POV: Mirabel. Beat: prickly chemistry; two people who'd rather be alone choosing not to be.

chapters.title: First Key: The Carousel Gate
chapters.summary: The first key opens a maintenance hatch behind the gym, revealing a corridor lined with old park signage. Inside, someone has left fresh chalk arrows — Juniper's handwriting. POV: alternating Mirabel/Theo. Beat: wonder curdling into dread; she went down here on purpose.

chapters.title: Tryouts for a Team That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: To stay close to the investigation, Mirabel joins the quiz team Theo captains, shocking everyone including herself. Coach Voss, a former Meridian employee, watches her with recognition. POV: Mirabel. Beat: comic relief and found-family seeds among misfit teammates.

chapters.title: Second Key: The Hall of Mirrors
chapters.summary: A key opens a bricked funhouse wing where mirrors show the rooms as they were forty years ago. In one reflection, Mirabel sees Juniper walking away from her. POV: Mirabel. Beat: grief and obsession entwining; the past is literally visible.

chapters.title: Coach Voss's Story
chapters.summary: Voss confesses: she was there the night founder Elias Meridian disappeared during the park's closing gala, and Juniper is Elias's great-granddaughter — heir to whatever he hid below. POV: Voss (flashback frame). Beat: the weight of inheritance; secrets kept too long.

chapters.title: Third Key: The Ticket Booth
chapters.summary: The third key fits a ticket booth preserved under the library, dispensing one admission stub printed with tomorrow's date. Theo admits his family were Meridian's rivals, bought out and silenced. POV: Theo. Beat: betrayal of legacy; loyalty tested against bloodline duty.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Quiz regionals: Mirabel's quick recall wins the match, but mid-victory she recognizes a question about Meridian Park that only someone from inside could have written. Someone is watching her through the competition. POV: Mirabel. Beat: triumph undercut by paranoia.

chapters.title: Fourth Key: The Flooded Tunnel
chapters.summary: A key opens a flooded tunnel beneath the pool; wading through, they find Juniper's jacket and a recording — her voice explaining she found Elias's vault and someone sealed her in to keep it shut. POV: Theo. Beat: terror and urgency; this is now a rescue.

chapters.title: The Rival Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Quiz rival Dana Ashford reveals she's been leaving clues too — her grandmother was Elias's business partner, cheated out of everything. Three heirs, three legacies, one vault. POV: Dana. Beat: enemies becoming allies; found family widening.

chapters.title: Fifth Key: The Manager's Office
chapters.summary: The fifth key opens Elias's office, frozen mid-decision, with a ledger showing the 'inheritance' isn't money — it's the deed to everything beneath the school, and a choice: reopen the park or bury it deeper. POV: Mirabel. Beat: love against duty takes shape.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone reports the team's study sessions; Mirabel nearly loses eligibility. Mr. Sable quietly restores her standing — he's been guarding the tunnels since the night Elias vanished. POV: Sable. Beat: unexpected guardianship; the adults choose her side.

chapters.title: Sixth Key: The Gala Floor
chapters.summary: Beneath the auditorium lies the intact ballroom where the last gala ended mid-song. Dust-covered glasses, a stopped clock, and the seventh keyhole waiting on the stage. POV: Mirabel. Beat: awe and dread converging; the finale is close.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: The championship that doesn't matter becomes the one that does: winning earns the team access to the auditorium sublevel during finals weekend, when the school is empty. They win by one question — about Meridian Park. POV: Theo. Beat: earned victory, nerves strung tight.

chapters.title: Seventh Key: The Vault
chapters.summary: Finals weekend. The seventh key turns. Inside the vault: Elias alive in suspended stasis he built himself, and Juniper beside him, keeping him company, unharmed. He sealed himself away rather than let his heirs fight over the park. POV: Mirabel. Beat: relief crashing into moral complexity.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Elias offers Mirabel the inheritance — she's descended from his partner, the true co-founder. Taking it means reopening the park and uprooting the school; refusing buries Juniper's discovery forever. Theo and the others stand with her either way. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the choice that defines her.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Before the final buzzer, Mirabel announces her decision at center court: the land goes to a community trust — the park reopened above, the school honored below, no single heir owning the past. Elias, freed, signs it willingly. POV: Mirabel. Beat: courage made public; duty redefined as shared.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Juniper comes home, furious and forgiven, and makes Mirabel a new mixtape titled ENCORE. The carousel gate becomes a public entrance; the team celebrates in the reopened ballroom. POV: Juniper. Beat: joy, restitution, friendship sealed.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mirabel's POV. Graduation day on the restored midway. She keeps the key ring — not as inheritance, but as a promise. Theo takes her hand as the carousel starts turning again. Beat: quiet, earned hope; the story ends with music playing.
